notes.title: Bebop Grand Clash: TBT Edition - Tournament Recap
notes.content: [p]Our latest [b]South Pole Bebop[/b] tournament, [b]Bebop Grand Clash: TBT Edition[/b], wrapped up a little over a week ago - and what a month it was. Across three weekends of fierce matches, clever plays, and some genuinely unexpected twists, we saw exactly what makes the SPB community special: creativity, strategy, and a whole lot of heart.[/p][p]Held during the [url="https://turnbasedfest.com/"]Turn-Based Thursday Fest 2025[/url], this event brought together new players, tournament veterans, and content creators for an international competition with a prize pool designed to reward both skill and participation. We’re proud to say it was our most exciting tournament yet.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]A Format That Put Players First[/b][/h3][p]This year, we wanted to try something different. Bebop Grand Clash was designed to be [b]more strategic and more watchable[/b] - so we introduced [b]Open Decklists[/b], used Discord for real-time spectating, and brought back some of our most dedicated community members as seeded players.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]📅 Tournament Schedule:[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]Preliminaries[/b]: June 7–8[/p][/*][*][p][b]Quarterfinals[/b]: June 21–22[/p][/*][*][p][b]Semifinals[/b]: June 28[/p][/*][*][p][b]Finals[/b]: June 29[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/dcc51deca59cc02c3de132cfcd1cfde4436441f1.png"][/img][/p][p]We had [b]14 players[/b] in total - some who found us through Tokyo Game Show, others who’ve played in every major tournament we’ve run. The bracket featured a mix of newcomers and six “seeds,” players known for their consistent competitive presence:[/p][p][b]gamedalgona[/b], [b]iaur64[/b], [b]nabug[/b], [b]bkindtoevery1[/b], [b]nijimath[/b], and [b]kamaqra[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Feature: Open Decklists[/b][/h3][p]For the first time, we made decklists public before each stage. Players submitted two decks in advance, and had to declare which one they’d use for each match. This turned every round into a real mind game - with no surprises, the spotlight was entirely on [b]decision-making and adaptation[/b].[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/967e98c90f4813dcd6d2f1e7a15bbdd4f7026dc8.png"][/img][/p][p]Spoiler: it worked. Matches felt tighter, reads were sharper, and viewers got a deeper look into how SPB plays at a high level.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Lobby Creator? Let the Wheel Decide[/b][/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/0ec7acbc44823c0444e8e02c8a4a8dc2363b4095.png"][/img][/p][p]To keep things fair (and a little unpredictable), we used a spin-wheel randomizer to determine who would create the match lobby in each pair. In [i]South Pole Bebop[/i], the player who sets up the lobby typically takes the first turn — a small edge that can make a big difference in the right hands. So rather than flipping coins, we let fate (and the wheel) decide.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Broadcast, Community & Discord Magic[/b][/h3][p]We streamed every round of the tournament on [url="https://www.youtube.com/@sentience-games/streams"]YouTube[/url], [url="https://www.twitch.tv/southpolebebop"]Twitch[/url], and our [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2184470/South_Pole_Bebop/"]Steam Page[/url], accompanied by insightful commentary and active chat. But a lot of the real magic happened on [b]Discord[/b] - where players screen-shared their games live in dedicated voice channels.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/be81ac395957043eb503f43ab10bb75c086e946b.png"][/img][/p][p]This meant spectators could jump in and watch unfiltered matches in real time, while players stayed in touch directly with moderators, and other competitors.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/ca273a9987f01e83b141bcd2ed36a0d0adeb59da.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Final Rankings[/b][/h3][p]After several hard-fought rounds, the finals came down to [b]Gamedalgona[/b] and [b]Iaur64[/b] — two players who’ve been in the mix since our earliest days. The final was a best-of-three and delivered the kind of tight tactical play that defines South Pole Bebop at its best.[/p][p][i](”@” - a reference to the participants’ Discord name)[/i][/p][p]🏆 [b]1st – @gamedalgona[/b][/p][p]🥈 [b]2nd – @iaur64[/b][/p][p]🥉 [b]3rd – @あじのり[/b][/p][p]🎖️ [b]4th – @nabug[/b][/p][p][b]Prizes included[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]A [b]Steam Deck 1TB[/b] (or Nintendo Switch 2) for the winner[/p][/*][*][p]$200, $100, and $50 Steam Gift Cards for runners-up[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Community Mini Events: Cheer & Predictions[/b][/h3][p]To keep things fun for spectators, we ran two smaller community events during the tournament:[/p][list][*][p][b]Cheer Message Winner[/b] – @Umbrița, for dropping kind and hilarious messages across the stream and Discord[/p][/*][*][p][b]Champion Prediction Winner[/b] – @宮村, who correctly predicted the winner (one of only five who did!)[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/1a3ab85b6f5d932b6f2203e4722bae2341a27446.png"][/img][/p][p]Both earned bonus Steam gift cards — perfect timing for the Summer Sale.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Aftermath: Feedback and Impression[/b][/h3][p]We hope that both players and viewers had a great time, as they shared plenty of positive feedback and showed great sportsmanship throughout.[/p][p]Here are just a few quotes from participants:[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/cf3dd0db8708eeae2336cfb1a6aa4eba810440ee.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Missed It? Watch the Tournament Here:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]🎥 [url="https://www.youtube.com/@sentience-games/streams" style="button"]Full VODs[/url][/p][/*][*][p]🌟 [url="https://youtu.be/bNa3o-DVjYs?si=x3WQ1ZPU8fH55x5T" style="button" buttoncolor="#006475"]Highlight Videos[/url] (we're adding more daily)[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]What’s Next?[/b][/h3][p]We’re already thinking about the next tournament. Whether you’re a casual fan or top-tier competitor, there’ll be more opportunities to join in![/p][p]📌 [b]Want to participate in the next one?[/b][/p][p]Follow us on [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2184470"]Steam[/url] and [url="https://discord.gg/XevW2Cjcyn"]join our Discord[/url]. That’s where sign-ups, rule changes, and early info always go first.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Thanks again to everyone who played, watched, predicted, streamed, cheered, or helped organize the Bebop Grand Clash: TBT Edition. This game wouldn’t be what it is without your support - and we’re just getting started.[/p][p]See you in the next match![/p]

notes.title: Update 0.12 (The biggest update ever!)
notes.content:
It's been over 6 months since the last v0.9 version update dev log! (Consistency is really challenging) Now it's a jump from v0.9 to v0.12 update. And as you can imagine, [i]it is big.[/i]
We're incredibly excited to reopen the [b]demo[/b] to introduce you to our new systems.

[h2]TUTORIAL IS FINALLY HERE[/h2]
Finally, the tutorial stage is here. The most requested feature, right? 
You can check it out by clicking the 'TUTORIAL' signpost in the main menu. Now, anyone new to the game can experience the tutorial and start playing! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/cecbca7b2e2b09038842f5983877bbdfe06a5328.png[/img]

For those who are already familiar with the game, I recommend you to give it a try... There's an opening scene explaining why zombies are emerging from the ground. (Spoiler alert: featuring the perfect combo, Mahana and Maka)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/cc182d16f5dfc956a260c74b5f4acd37aa84ed29.gif[/img]

[h2]DECKBUILDING[/h2]
In the version 0.9, we used to accumulate experience points (XP) to level up and upgrade characters, but now this has been transformed into a "card deck-building" element. You can set up to [b]15 cards[/b] for character upgrades, base upgrades, and magic cards from the main menu. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/31396e95ba4f932ee8fc9db3f37f18c61dc3debd.gif[/img]
You can purchase cards using the "cores" you've collected through leveling up in the game. Using cards at the right time is important, but it's also crucial to decide which combination of cards to take with you from the beginning of the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/21b084700e3b29642d0795314e7fc839ce8957c8.png[/img]

[h2]LIFEHOLD AND ICEKEEP[/h2]
In the version 0.9, there were two bases that needed to be protected; now one is Lifehold, which is related to your life, and the other is Icekeep, which is related to experience points (XP). If the Lifehold, where the penguins' food (sardine) is stored, is destroyed, the game ends. If the Icekeep, the ice storage, are destroyed, the opponent gains a large amount of XP. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/76d9bccccd804ca29facda46fece3ef56f7fc5dc.gif[/img]

[h2]ONE MORE?[/h2]
Now it's enough to start playing the game. But if you want to [i]really [/i]play the game in a truly hardcore manner, there's one more thing to know!
[b]Double Turn:[/b] If one of your characters dies, you'll use one of the remaining characters again. However, the character doing the Double Turn will have both their attack power and movement distance reduced by one. If you couldn't protect your character, you'll have to accept this much. (Heh)
In addition, there are now purple [b]tooltips [/b]available, so you can find more detailed information by hovering your mouse over each UI element. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43188750/638e338bcc9a8706e3cfb9d6386ec182c956110b.png[/img]

Of course, feel free to ask devs on [url=https://discord.gg/Q3dMeqX2gb]Discord[/url] if you have any questions! 

Actually, there are many more backlog update logs, but I'll take the time to explain them in detail next time if I have the opportunity. I'll cover why certain systems were implemented and how to use them, etc. 

[h2]SOUTH POLE BEBOP LEAGUE EVENT?[/h2]
Recently, we held an in-house mini-league. Well...the victory went to the mighty game designer, but it was also a time for bug fixes, balancing adjustments, and discovering more about the game's fun factor. A fierce (literally) scene unfolded with a $50 prize at stake → https://x.com/southpolebebop/status/1766027174073840114?s=20 

I'm eager to host league matches with players (please no more with devs.)
[h3][b][url=https://discord.gg/Q3dMeqX2gb]Anyone up for it?[/url][/b][/h3] 
The follow-up instructions will be primarily through Discord, so if you'd like to participate, join us on Discord! 
Show off your skills in the new version of South Pole Bebop ✌️


Alright, alright, that's it for today.
Stay tuned for the next update dev log, coming in..who knows when. 🐧👋

notes.title: Update 0.85
notes.content:
[h3][New Characters !] [/h3]
"HOPU"  The Adelie Penguin uses Judo Martial Arts 🐧🥋 
You can grab enemies and throw them over your shoulder.

"MOMONA" is a plump seal with a big appetite. 
You can charge at enemies from a distance.

"TONY SEALPRANO" is the boss of the Antarctic seal MAFIA. 🦭🎩 
You can charm enemies and draw them in.

[h3][New Zombie !] [/h3]
"Boomer" is a zombie that explodes when touched. 💥
Unlike other zombies, if you PUSH it, it flies far away.
Try playing ping-pong with each other, like a ping-pong ball.

[h3][New Level Up System]🏅[/h3]
Now, when you level up, characters can purchase individual bonuses in a newly renovated system.
Also, each character can purchase special upgrades.
For example, when you upgrade KAWAU, its attack will penetrate objects!

[h3][Other Improvements] 🗒️[/h3]
1) Game background and other graphic resources have been upgraded.
2) Distinction between allies and enemies is clearer. Now, allies are marked in green and enemies in red.
3) Zombie attacks are now more visible in terms of their direction.
4) The animations of the characters have become more diverse.
5) The AI has become stronger 🤖


Thank you for waiting!
Until now, updates have been made only through internal testing to establish a stable development environment.
In celebration of the upcoming Steam Next Fest, a lot of new content has been added, so enjoy the new game with your friends! 🥳

notes.title: Update 0.4
notes.content:
[h2][New System][/h2]
[h3]" 'vs AI Bot' mode has been added!":robot:[/h3]
> Was it difficult to play because there were few game users? Now, 'AI Bot' has been added to the game so that you can enjoy the game even without an opponent. It's still only a simple level AI, but we plan to provide AI with a higher level of difficulty by gradually upgrading the AI.
> But remember! Mindgame is more fun with real people.

[h2][UX improvements][/h2]
[h3]"When an enemy attacks, the amount of damage is displayed."📈[/h3]
By clicking on the character, you could see the status, such as attack power, but it was inconvenient.
Now you can instantly know how much damage a zombie or opponent is doing when they attack.

[h3]"Added zombie timer":timer:[/h3]
There were comments that the timer at the top of the screen always had the same shape, making it difficult to tell the turn of the zombies.
Now, when the zombie moves, a nice snurgle animation is displayed instead of a timer.

The game's UX is constantly being improved based on your feedback.
We are working hard on additional content such as new characters, so please look forward to the next update!

notes.title: Update 0.3
notes.content:
[h2]New Contents[/h2]
[h3]- "A new zombie has been added that fires from a distance" 💣 [/h3]
The new zombie "Head Bomber" can ignore terrain and shell targets from a long distance, just like MAKA.
Make sure your base isn't getting shelled!


[h2]improvements of UX[/h2]
[h3]- "You can now see your surroundings when selecting a level-up bonus" 🎉 [/h3]
In the previous version, all objects except your character were hidden on the screen where you select level-up bonuses, making it difficult to see what was going on around you.
Now, instead of hiding, we've added an effect that makes the surrounding objects look darker, so you can see what's going on around you and better see the character you're giving the bonus to.


[h3]- "Showing a before and after of a character's improving stats" 📈 [/h3]
Originally, we used to show the improved stats above your character, but it was too quick for users to notice.
Now, we've made it more intuitive by showing a before and after, such as "2->3", when a character's stats improve.

[h3]- "It's always shown whose turn it is" ❓ 
[/h3]With no battle log yet, it's hard to know if it's your turn or your opponent's turn when you lose focus on the game for a while.
We've changed this to show whose turn it is by adding a flashing effect under the profile of the user whose turn it is.

[h3]- "We've added cutscenes to help guide you through the game" 🎥. [/h3]
   1) Added a cutscene at the start of the game that tells you the result of your starting order (first/last turn). 
   2) Added an illustration that appears when your character is captured by Grabby.
   3) Added a cutscene that tells you what to do when your base is destroyed to either solidify your victory or avoid losing.



[h2]- Other improvements[/h2]
1) Added button flashing effect when leveling up.
2) Added effects of attacks and explosions.
3) Several UI visualizations have been changed.

notes.title: Update 0.2
notes.content:
-[h3][b] "Added VFX for zombies falling into water." [/b] [/h3]
Until now, pushing a zombie towards water would cause the zombie to float on top of the water. Zombies now fall into the water.

-[h3] [b]"The resource the character is swimming in has been added.[/b] 🤽‍♂️ '"[/h3]
Unlike zombies, player characters do not die when they enter a water tile. (cannot attack instead)
However, even if the character fell into the water, the appearance did not change, so it was difficult to immediately know what effect the water tile had.
Now, when your character enters a water tile, it will appear to be swimming.

- [h3][b]" Added VFX when acquiring EXP. 🎇 "[/b][/h3]
The 'how' to get the experience was explained through the tooltip. However, the 'process' of acquiring experience seemed unclear.
VFX have now been added to show "where" and "how much" XP earned.
 
-[h3] [b]"(Convenience up) The game can now be played with just a mouse without a keyboard 🖱️" [/b][/h3]
Now you don't have to press Space to attack. All actions can be performed with the mouse.
